services.title: Services
services.intro: We start from needs, not a product catalogue. Below we describe how we work when the assignment is a solution, a team or specialist reinforcement.

i1.title: Defined assignments
i1.body: From requirements and plan to execution and handover. You get clear deliverables, documentation and acceptance points.

i2.title: Team delivery
i2.body: A coordinated team with a shared plan, status reporting and ownership of the whole delivery.

i3.title: Specialist reinforcement
i3.body: When you need complementary competence inside your existing organization — with a clear role and follow-up.

i4.title: Integrations and further development
i4.body: When existing systems need to be connected, modernized or extended — with documentation that can be operated.

services.closing: Technology choices follow the assignment’s requirements. We describe solutions in terms of need, risk and operability — not trendy tool lists.

publicSector.title: Public sector
publicSector.intro: Public organizations need clarity, traceability and long-term operations. Here we describe practices we work by — without legal or contractual claims.

items.c1: Requirements and scope are documented before execution.
items.c2: Status and deviations are communicated in writing and on time.
items.c3: Deliverables are tied to acceptance criteria where relevant.
items.c4: Documentation must be hand-overable to your organization.
items.c5: Security and access are handled according to an agreed model.
items.c6: Operations and further development are planned during delivery.
items.c7: We avoid publishing claims about frameworks, ISO or references without verification.

publicSector.note: This page is not legal advice and does not replace your procurement documents.
publicSector.statement: Clarity, traceability and operability — practices that can be followed up during the contract period.

delivery.title: Delivery capability
delivery.intro: Our model follows five stages. Each stage has concrete deliverables so the assignment can be ordered, followed up and operated. This is a working model — not a proprietary brand.

s1.title: Anchor
s1.body: Need, goals, roles and mandate are clarified before execution.
s1.deliverables: Needs description, roles, scope boundary, initial risk list.

s2.title: Plan
s2.body: Commitment, risk, time, quality and acceptance are defined so the assignment can be followed up.
s2.deliverables: Commitment description, plan, communication and acceptance model.

s3.title: Execute
s3.body: Transparent status, documented decisions and controlled changes during the work.
s3.deliverables: Ongoing status, decision points, change log.

s4.title: Follow up
s4.body: Quality, deviations, actions and reporting are summarized visibly.
s4.deliverables: Follow-up record, deviation handling, remaining items.

s5.title: Secure continuity
s5.body: Handover, competence sharing, operations and improvement are planned so delivery can continue.
s5.deliverables: Handover package, operating routines, contact points.

delivery.visualizationBody: Timelines, quality gates and documentation trails create transparency throughout the delivery.
delivery.riskBody: Risk is reduced through early scoping, visible status and handover-ready documentation — not by promising more than the assignment allows.

quality.title: Quality and security
quality.intro: Here we describe how we work with quality, information security and follow-up in digital assignments — as practices, not certification claims.

q1.title: Traceability
q1.body: Requirements, decisions and changes are documented so they can be followed during the assignment.

q2.title: Deviation handling
q2.body: Deviations are communicated on time, with action and follow-up.

q3.title: Documentation
q3.body: Documentation must be hand-overable and usable in your organization.

q4.title: Robust digital services
q4.body: We plan for operability, access control and controlled change.

quality.note: We do not list ISO certificates, clearances or frameworks without documented verification.

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: Choose what works for you. We use Calendly for booking so you get confirmation immediately.
contact.bookBody: A short introduction call via Calendly. No contact form on the site — we avoid uncertain personal-data handling on static hosting.

afterItems.a1: You receive a confirmation from Calendly.
afterItems.a2: We prepare based on the information you share in the booking.
afterItems.a3: The call covers needs, scope and possible next steps — without manufactured urgency.

contact.noEmailNote: A company address on our own domain will be published when verified. Personal emails are not shown as the company address.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This page describes how A2M Tech AB handles personal data in connection with the website and contact.
privacy.collectBody: Via Calendly you may provide name, email and other information you enter. If you call us, we process the data needed to respond. There is no contact form on the website.
privacy.purposeBody: To answer inquiries, book meetings and discuss potential assignments.
privacy.shareBody: Booking uses Calendly (third party). LinkedIn is used if you choose to contact us there. We do not sell personal data.
privacy.analyticsBody: Web analytics is off by default. If analytics is enabled in the future, it will require explicit consent.
privacy.rightsBody: You may request access, rectification or erasure under applicable law. Contact us by phone or Calendly.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.intro: a2m-tech.com is a static website. We do not use tracking cookies by default.
cookies.necessaryBody: Technically necessary browser functions and any language preference you control via navigation. No cookie banner is shown when no analytics runs.
cookies.analyticsBody: No web analytics is enabled in the default setup. If analytics is introduced, it will be consent-gated.
cookies.thirdBody: Links to Calendly and LinkedIn may lead to services that set their own cookies under their terms.
